findings.basis: The index records no family, but all five profiles come from the lineage-device-carrier-overlays candidates (the 311-00 profile also from sony-open-devices-aosp). Profiles 310-01, 310-02, 310-88 and 311-00 come from the Qualcomm/CAF CarrierConfig vendor.xml that 6 to 83 LineageOS device trees copy (for example oneplus_benz vendor.xml:2371-2398, 2436-2449, 2735-2742). These blocks use two-digit MNCs under MCC 310/311. US networks use three-digit MNCs. Android takes a two-digit MNC only when the SIM's EF_AD says so, and otherwise uses three for 310 (IccRecords.java:634-662). So these blocks match only lab or test SIMs, not a commercial carrier. Google has no entry for them (google_entries empty), and the Google lane serves the Google default entry's false (000000.default.*.json). Profile 310-300 with GID1 2AC9 comes from one file, motorola sm7250-common vendor.xml:15267-15287. GID1 2AC9 is Consumer Cellular (AOSP carrier_list.textpb), and 310-300 is T-Mobile US's network (carrier ID 1). That Motorola file sets false in its other 2AC9 blocks on T-Mobile networks (310-160, 310-200 to 310-250, 310-270, 310-310, 310-660 and 310-800; the 310-260 block leaves it unset). The 310-300 true looks copied from Motorola's plain 310-300 block (vendor.xml:2231-2250), where VoLTE is unavailable and the value has no effect. The host carrier's own settings say false: AOSP carrier_config_carrierid_1_T-Mobile-US.xml:10, Google tmobile_us (the Google lane serves false), and the legacy frameworks/base values-mcc310-mnc300 overlay. So no profile has a basis that is a confirmed real carrier setting for this key.
findings.effect: The key decides whether a call made while TTY mode is on may use IMS on LTE/NR, and so whether it goes over VoLTE or to CS. Platform: ImsManager.isNonTtyOrTtyOnVolteEnabled() is true when the key is true or the current TTY mode is OFF (ImsManager.java:709-724). When it is false, reevaluateCapabilities() and setTtyMode() disable MMTEL voice and video on LTE and NR (ImsManager.java:1751-1756, 1830-1855, 2882-2900), so ImsPhone stops reporting VoLTE and GsmCdmaPhone.useImsForCall() sends the call to CS (GsmCdmaPhone.java:1235-1241, 1346-1347). Emergency: domain selection is off on this phone (empty config_domain_selection_service_component_name, packages/services/Telephony/res/values/config.xml:393; the phone log shows DomainSelectionResolver componentName=[], S20 report line 264), so the legacy path applies. GsmCdmaPhone.useImsForEmergency() requires isNonTtyOrTtyOnVolteEnabled() (GsmCdmaPhone.java:1243-1252). With true, an emergency call in TTY mode is placed over IMS (ImsPhone.dial, GsmCdmaPhone.java:1422-1428) and, with false, on CS. The key also feeds GsmCdmaPhone.isImsUseEnabled(), and because of operator precedence it gates the Wi-Fi calling branch there as well (GsmCdmaPhone.java:4370-4377). The domain selectors use the same key (EmergencyCallDomainSelector.java:755-756, NormalCallDomainSelector.java:372-382), but they are inactive here. AOSP ImsStack: CallFeature.isTtySupported() reads the key, with default false (CallFeature.java:80-83). Only when it is true does ImsCallContext create a TtyModeTracker (ImsCallContext.java:275-286) and setGttInfo() put the TTY mode into the call's media as GTT (ImsCallSessionImpl.java:1925-1960). Native GTT is a T.140 text stream (MtcMediaUtil.cpp:284-305, MtcMediaManager.cpp:347). The native TTY deregistration in AosCondition.cpp:813-826 and 1026-1031 is never reached, because AosService.notifyTtySetting() has no production caller in the tree or in the ocd fork. The media run on AOSP ImsMedia (STATUS.md:25), which carries T.140 text but has no Baudot or TTY-tone conversion. A wired TTY device's tones would only reach the IMS call as AMR audio, while the negotiated text stream stays empty. On CS, the modem receives the TTY mode through setTTYMode (GsmCdmaPhone.java:4128-4152). Settings UI: AccessibilitySettingsFragment.java:203-235 allows the TTY mode to be changed during a call only when this key is true. The phone runs 24.0 and the tree is 23.2; ImsManager and GsmCdmaPhone on 24.0 were not read.
findings.risk: With true instead of the Google lane's false, a call made in TTY mode, a 911 TTY call included, moves from CS onto VoLTE through AOSP ImsStack and ImsMedia. There, TTY works only as GTT/T.140 text, and nothing on this phone converts a TTY device's Baudot tones into that text. So the TTY conversation may not reach the PSAP or the relay service, or may arrive garbled as tones in AMR audio. For 310-300 with GID1 2AC9, it also places TTY calls over IMS on a T-Mobile network whose own configuration says TTY over VoLTE is not supported. The false that would otherwise be served keeps TTY calls on CS, where the modem handles TTY. No test can place a TTY or emergency call to check the IMS path.

notes: Hold. The key decides whether a TTY call, an emergency TTY call included, goes over VoLTE or to CS on this ROM (ImsManager capability gating, and GsmCdmaPhone.useImsForEmergency on the legacy path, because domain selection is off). On AOSP ImsStack with ImsMedia, the IMS side of TTY is T.140 text with no Baudot conversion, so true moves TTY calls onto a path that is not shown to work. The value's basis is weak. Four profiles are Qualcomm lab or test PLMN blocks (two-digit MNCs under 310/311, no carrier behind them, no Google entry). The fifth, Consumer Cellular on T-Mobile 310-300, comes from one Motorola file, is inconsistent within that file, and contradicts T-Mobile's own AOSP and Google settings (false). CarrierSettings should keep serving the Google lane's false.
